story.titleZh: 决定马德里首场F1比赛的5大因素
story.summaryZh: F1今日在马德里马德里赛道赛道迎来首场比赛，练习赛、排位赛及F2/F3垫场赛提供了一些线索，但缺乏历史数据意味着比赛仍可能充满意外。
story.originalTitle: 5 factors that will dictate Madrid's first F1 race
story.summaryEn: Formula 1 heads into the unknown today at the new Madring circuit in Madrid for its first Spanish Grand Prix, with practice, qualifying and support races offering some clues but no racing history meaning surprises are possible.
detailZh: F1各车队和车手在今日的西班牙大奖赛中驶入未知领域，因为这是大奖赛赛车首次在新马德里赛道赛道比赛。这意味着比赛将如何展开存在一些重大疑问，但已有指向潜在答案的线索。
练习赛和排位赛设定了一些预期，F2和F3垫场赛的进行方式也是如此，但这里缺乏可供参考的比赛历史，意味着可能会出现一些意外。
以下是可能影响比赛的五个关键方面。
截至撰写本文时，在马德里赛道举行的五场比赛——两场F2和三场F3——中，第二位发车有四次在起步时取得领先。在周日的F2和F3比赛中，两次都是杆位车手迅速向左移动，以覆盖第二位车手更强的起步。
从电视观众视角看，杆位在左侧，这符合惯例，因为它提供了弯道通常的赛车线，第二位在右侧。
可以肯定，迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯会非常清楚杆位是否存在任何劣势，这可能意味着他会认识到需要覆盖安东内利。不过，迈凯伦通常良好的起步也可能抵消任何劣势。
发车格不同侧的抓地力往往存在差异，而且每一排也可能不同，但本周末第二位发车位的抓地力比杆位略好一些。这可能意味着安东内利在起步时有机会，而诺里斯需要根据起步情况考虑覆盖他。
马德里赛道的主要超车点是5/5a/6号减速弯，它位于2号弯后长直全油门路段之后，会颠簸路肩。
这在垫场赛中产生了最多的轮对轮较量，但大多数情况导致一辆车、偶尔两辆车切弯。正如乔治·拉塞尔所说，“设计上的一个小遗憾是缺乏清晰的超车机会”，这意味着这个减速弯将是任何人最好的机会。
“总的来说，比赛中超车会非常困难，”红牛的利亚姆·劳森说。
“在那里防守很容易，或者比普通弯道更容易，因为你只需把对方推出减速弯，他就必须归还位置。”
这意味着会有大量无线电抱怨、许多沮丧的进攻，以及在战斗中出错时可能发生碰撞或撞墙。
或者，正如亚历克斯·阿尔本所说，“如果你看了F3和F2比赛，全是车手在减速弯并排，然后抱怨其中一人没有让他们重新超过。”
轮胎退化——包括前轮颗粒化和后轮过热——一直是西班牙大奖赛周末的主要话题之一。
情况已从周五练习赛大幅改善，当时乔治·拉塞尔半开玩笑地说马德里赛道的比赛看起来要进站六次。
事实上，随着赛道橡胶化相当好，现在一停和二停之间在时间上看起来相当微妙。
因此，由于超车似乎很困难，这意味着车队可能倾向于告诉车手管理轮胎，走保守路线以尽量减少进站。
但这对于处理过热轮胎来说都很好；阻止颗粒化则要困难得多。因此，颗粒化的程度可能将是关键。
当被问及比赛会混乱还是平淡时，奥迪的尼科·霍肯伯格说：“看，这真的取决于我们是否出现颗粒化，我认为那将是主要驱动因素。”
“如果我们出现颗粒化，我认为那会相当严重，可能会很混乱。但就像你说的，你知道，你永远不知道。”
颗粒化可能引发转向不足，使高速弯变得非常困难，并引发退化水平迅速上升——带来一些策略复杂性。
所以所有目光都需要关注左前轮胎。
鉴于需要保护轮胎并可能勉强完成一停，安东内利建议“前10圈将是奶奶式驾驶”，而马克斯·维斯塔潘说“你需要依赖别人轮胎退化得非常严重”。
那么，这是否意味着这可能是一场领先者——无论是全场领先还是车群领先——可以大幅减速并轻松挡住一串赛车的比赛？
这是一条防守容易的赛道，用去年的赛车肯定会出现这种情况。
然而，由于能量部署因素，现在有可能利用巨大的动力优势在不太可能的地方完成超车，这意味着如果你过于执着于阻挡对手，你会更加脆弱。
但即使这样做机会也有限，因为有些全油门区域很容易挡住后面的车——昨天卡洛斯·塞恩斯在通往7号弯的上坡路段无意中阻挡瓦尔特利·博塔斯就说明了这一点。
回顾阿塞拜疆大奖赛的历史表明，比赛的特点往往取决于车手的集体心态。
当预测会混乱时——正如巴库多次发生的那样——车手可以改变方法。他们选择稳妥行事，感觉到远离他人的麻烦就能保证积分。
这种策略很好。然而，当每个人都这样做时，结果可能是一种平静，导致比赛沉闷。
凯迪拉克车手瓦尔特利·博塔斯认为，马德里赛道有可能不会带来其布局暗示的不可预测性——就像第一次练习赛零中断那样。
“就像FP1，如果人们太谨慎，那就会发生，”他说。
“但你永远不知道。就是这样的赛道：一个错误就会黄旗、安全车或红旗，所以肯定会有人犯错。”
尽管巴库在混乱与平静之间摇摆的例子，查尔斯·勒克莱尔认为最终马德里会介于两者之间。
“我不会用那些极端，但当然我不知道混乱方面，”他说。
“我认为在这样具有挑战性的赛道上可能会有一些红旗或事故。然而，巴库在超车方面可能相当疯狂，而在这里，我很难看到很多很多超车。”
detailEn: Formula 1’s teams and drivers head into the unknown in today’s Spanish Grand Prix as it’s the first time grand prix cars have raced at the new Madring. And that means there are some big questions about how the race will unfold, but with signposts to the potential answers.

Practice and qualifying have set some expectations, as has the way the Formula 2 and Formula 3 support races have played out, but the lack of racing history here to go on means that there could be some surprises.
Here are five key aspects that could shape the race.

In the five Madring races held at the time of writing - two Formula 2 and three Formula 3 races - second on the grid has taken the lead at the start four times. And in Sunday’s F2 and F3 races, on both occasions the polesitter moved left quickly to cover the stronger start of the driver in second.
Pole position is on the left side as the TV viewer looks at it, which is as per convention as it gives the usual racing line for the corner, with second on the right.

You can be certain that McLaren's Lando Norris will be very well aware if there is any disadvantage to being on pole position, potentially meaning he will recognise the need to cover Antonelli. Then again, it might be that McLaren's generally good launches offset any disadvantage.

There is often a difference in grip on different sides of the grid, as well as the potential for it varying depending on each row, but this weekend the second-placed grid slot has got a little more grip than pole position. That could mean an opportunity for Antonelli at the start, and the need for Norris to consider covering him depending on how the launch goes.
The main passing place at the Madring is the kerb-rattling Turn 5/5a/6 chicane that follows the long flat-out blast from Turn 2.

This has produced the most wheel-to-wheel action in the support races, but with the majority of instances resulting in one, or occasionally both, cars cutting the track. As George Russell put it, "the one small frustration in the design is the lack of clear overtaking opportunities", meaning the chicane is going to be the best chance anyone has.
"It's going to be very hard to overtake in the race in general," said Red Bull's Liam Lawson.
"It's very easy to defend there, or easier than normal corners, because you just push the guy off through the chicane and he has to give the place back."
This means there will be plenty of radio complaining, lots of frustrated attacks and the potential either for a collision or hitting the wall if you get it wrong in battle.
Or, as Alex Albon put it, "if you watched the F3 and F2 races, it was all drivers going side by side in the chicane and then complaining that one of them didn't let them back past."
Tyre degradation – both from front graining and rears overheating – has been one of the big talking points over the Spanish GP weekend.
The situation has improved a lot from Friday practice, when George Russell half-joked that the Madring race looked like it was heading for a six-stopper.
In fact, with the track having rubbered in quite well, things now look quite delicately poised time-wise between a one and a two-stopper.
So, with overtaking appearing to be difficult, that means the likely preference for teams will be to tell drivers to manage tyres and play the conservative route to minimise pit stops.
But that is all well and good for handling overheating tyres; stopping graining is a much harder task. Therefore, the level of graining will potentially be key.
As Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg said about whether the race would be chaotic or processional: “Look, it really depends, if we get graining, if we don't, I think that will be the main driver.
“If we get graining, I think it's going to be quite something and it might be chaotic. But, like you say, you know, you never know.”
Graining could trigger understeer, make the high-speed corners very difficult and trigger a rapid increase in degradation levels – throwing some strategy complications.
So all eyes need to be on those front-left tyres.

Given the need to protect the tyres and potentially eke out a one-stopper, Antonelli suggested "it's going to be grandmother driving in the first 10 laps", while Max Verstappen says "you need to rely on people [tyre] deg-ing very aggressively".
So does that mean this could be one of those races where the leader either of the race overall, or of a pack of cars, can back off dramatically and easily hold up a queue of cars?
It's a track where defending is easy, and with last year's cars it would definitely be on the cards.

However, with the deployment factor, it's now possible to use a huge power advantage to make a drive-by move in an unlikely place, meaning that you are more vulnerable if you are committing to holding up rivals too much.

But, there are limited opportunities even to do that as there are full-throttle zones where it’s easy to keep a car behind - Carlos Sainz inadvertently impeding Valtteri Bottas on the run up the hill to Turn 7 illustrated that yesterday.
A look back through the history of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix has shown that the characteristics of a race can often depend on the collective mindset of the drivers.

When chaos is predicted – as has happened many times in Baku – the drivers can change their approach. They opt to play it safe, sensing that staying out of everyone else’s trouble will guarantee points.
That tactic is all well and good. However, when everyone does it then the result can be a level of calmness that leads to a subdued race.
Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas thinks it is possible that Madring does not deliver the unpredictability that its layout hints at – as happened when opening practice threw up zero stoppages.
“Like FP1, if people are too cautious, then that can happen,” he said.
“But you just never know. It's a track like that: one mistake and it will be yellow or safety car or red flag, so surely somebody is going to make a mistake.”
Despite the example of Baku bouncing between chaos and calm, Charles Leclerc thinks in the end Madrid will be somewhere in the middle.
“I wouldn't use those extreme ends, but surely I don't know about the chaos in a way,” he said.

“I think there may be some red flags or some incidents on a track that is so challenging like this one. However, Baku can be quite crazy with overtakes, while here, I struggle to see many, many overtakes.”
keyPointsZh: 在马德里赛道已举行的五场F2/F3比赛中，第二位发车四次在起步时取得领先，且本周末第二位发车位的抓地力略优于杆位。
5/5a/6号减速弯是主要超车点，但多数轮对轮较量以切弯告终，乔治·拉塞尔称设计上缺乏清晰超车机会，利亚姆·劳森称防守容易。
轮胎颗粒化和后轮过热是周末焦点，一停与二停策略之间平衡微妙，尼科·霍肯伯格认为颗粒化将是比赛混乱与否的关键。
keyPointsEn: In the five F2/F3 races held at Madring, second on the grid took the lead at the start four times, and this weekend the second-placed grid slot has slightly more grip than pole position.

The Turn 5/5a/6 chicane is the main passing place, but most wheel-to-wheel action ended with track cutting; George Russell called the design's lack of clear overtaking opportunities a frustration, and Liam Lawson said defending is easy.

Tyre graining and rear overheating are weekend talking points, with the balance between a one- and two-stopper delicate; Nico Hulkenberg said graining will be the main driver of whether the race is chaotic.

relatedItems.titleZh: 博塔斯解释巴库站大幅落后佩雷兹的原因
relatedItems.summaryZh: 博塔斯透露，在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上他平均每圈比凯迪拉克队友佩雷兹慢超过1.7秒，是2026赛季迄今正赛中最大的队内差距，他对此表示在直道和弯角都无法跟上节奏。
relatedItems.originalTitle: The slowest race of F1 2026 explained
relatedItems.summaryEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed why he was on average more than 1.7 seconds per lap slower than his Cadillac team-mate Sergio Perez at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race-day intra-team deficit of the 2026 season so far.
detailZh: 瓦尔特里·博塔斯透露了上一站巴库比赛中，他相比凯迪拉克F1队友塞尔吉奥·佩雷兹速度严重不足的一些原因。
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，博塔斯平均每圈比佩雷兹慢超过1.7秒之多，这是2026赛季迄今正赛中最大的队内差距。甚至他的最快单圈也比佩雷兹慢1.489秒。
博塔斯在最后一圈撞上护墙，因为他在驶过1号弯逃生通道后，赛车的能量输出模式“有点混乱”，而由于多跑了距离，他在进入15号弯左弯时后刹车失效，车头撞上了护墙。
但更令人担忧的是此前惊人的速度差距，在博塔斯撞车之前，佩雷兹几乎已经套了他一圈。
“我理解从外面看起来情况很糟糕，坐在车里感觉也很糟糕，”博塔斯周四在马来西亚说。
“当时根本没办法跟上大部队。我在比赛中尝试了所有办法，也得到了很多关于我在哪里损失时间的反馈。很大一部分是在直道上，但也有相当大的一部分是在整圈的弯道中损失掉的。
“所以我一直在坚持推进直到最后，这也是为什么我在最后一圈进一号弯时锁死了轮胎。
“不过是的，关键问题是在练习中我们就已经看到我的速度不够。我无法像佩雷兹那样以同样的速度过弯，所以我们在排位赛前做了很多改动，包括一些减震器和底板，结果感觉确实好多了。
“但在正赛中，行驶品质又明显衰减了很多……我们这次改动了很多东西，所以我觉得问题在于减震器随温度衰减，还有底板……我们在某些地方仍然缺少一些压力测量点，所以对于气动部件，我还拿不到过去习惯获得的完整信息。
“通过数据你马上就能看出性能是提升还是下降，但现在底板有一些区域我们完全看不见。不过就我个人的感觉而言，更多问题出在行驶品质上——再加上动力转向整个周末都在不断衰减。所以我在整场比赛中真的很难去感受赛车。
“这些因素叠加在一起。而且动力单元的差距可能比我们预想的要大，至少从数据上看是这样。
“理论上我们有一个数字，但那是新引擎对全新引擎，也就是新规格对旧规格的对比。所以，我想就是这些因素叠加的结果。我当时确实相当慢。”
动力单元方面的差异指的是佩雷兹在巴库已经用上了升级版 ADUO 2 法拉利引擎，而博塔斯还没有。
此前这被描述为“细微差别”，但正如博塔斯所说，这次升级的效果可能比最初想象的更大。
博塔斯表示，他的 ADUO 2 引擎能否及时送到、让他能在雪邦赛道使用，可能性是“五五开”；如果赶不上，他就得等到下周的新加坡大奖赛。
他的队友佩雷兹本周末不会使用这套引擎，而是换用自己引擎池中的另一套动力单元，以便把升级版留到更能发挥作用的比赛周末再使用。
佩雷斯解释说：“我们做出了一个我们认为胜算最大的决定。”
“这就是为什么我们会在这里承受一些损失。但我们希望这会有所回报。”
“我们对这个周末并不太乐观。所以我们决定把它省下来。”
正如佩雷斯所暗示的，凯迪拉克的车手们已经为艰难的周末做好了准备，因为雪邦赛道带来了两个凯迪拉克尤其难以应对的挑战：轮胎过热和高速弯角。
正如佩雷兹所解释的，凯迪拉克目前“赛车的下压力严重不足，而且阻力很大”。
“在巴库，我基本上整场比赛都保持在超车模式上，所以才能跟住其他车手，”佩雷兹说。
“但当我超过他们之后，我就只能像个乘客一样，因为我没有直道速度。所以我们有两大问题：下压力不足和很大的阻力。”
“但我们一直都知道，第一年会很艰难。”
detailEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed some of the reasons behind his woeful lack of pace compared to Cadillac Formula 1 team-mate Sergio Perez last time out in Baku.

Bottas was on average over a whopping 1.7 seconds slower than Perez per lap at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race day intra-team deficit of 2026 so far. Even his single fastest lap was 1.489s slower than Perez.

Bottas ended up in the wall on the final lap as his car’s deployment pattern “got a bit confused” because he went down the Turn 1 escape road, then because of the extra distance travelled his rear brakes didn’t work going into the Turn 15 left-hander, where he nosed into the barriers.
But what was more worrying was the alarming lack of pace before then, with Perez close to lapping Bottas before the latter's crash.
“I understand it looked pretty bad from the outside and felt pretty bad in the car as well,” Bottas said on Thursday in Malaysia.

“There was just no way to keep up with the pack. I tried everything during the race, and got lots of feedback on where I am losing the time. A lot of it was on the straights, but also a big chunk was just all around the lap in the corners.
“That's why I just kept pushing until the end and that's why I had to lock up on the last lap into Turn 1.

“But yeah, the main thing was we saw already in practice that I was lacking pace. I couldn't carry the same speed through the corners as Checo, so we changed a lot for the qualifying, including some dampers and the floor, and it actually felt a lot better.

“But then the ride again during the race degraded quite a lot... Again, we've changed a lot of things, so I think it's something to do with dampers degging with heat, the floor... We are still lacking a bit of pressure tappings here and there, so we still don't have the full information on aero parts that I'm used to from the past.

“You can immediately see if you're down or up, but now there are some bits of the floor where we are blind. But for me, feeling-wise, it was more the ride - that, in combination with the power steering that was degging throughout the weekend. So I was really then also struggling to feel the car throughout the race.
“So those things combined. And then the [power unit] difference was probably bigger than we thought, at least from the data.
“We've got a number in theory, but that's new engine versus new one, of the new and old spec. So yeah, I think those combined. I was pretty slow.”
The power unit difference is in reference to Perez having the upgraded ADUO 2 Ferrari engine in Baku while Bottas doesn’t yet have it.
This was previously described as a “small difference”, but as Bottas says the upgrade may be more powerful than first thought.
Bottas says it’s “50/50” if his ADUO 2 engine arrives in time for him to run it at Sepang; if not, he’ll have to wait until next week in Singapore.
Team-mate Perez won’t be running it this weekend, swapping to a different power unit in his pool in order to save it for a weekend when it will be more beneficial.
“We took a decision where we feel we got the best shot at it,” Perez explained.
“That's why we're taking a bit of a hit here. But we hope that it will pay us back.
“We are not too optimistic about this weekend. So we decided to save it.”
As Perez alluded, the Cadillac drivers are braced for a difficult weekend because Sepang poses two challenges the Cadillac struggles with in particular: tyre overheating and high-speed corners.
As Perez explains, the Cadillac has “a massive lack of load in the car and a lot of drag” right now.
“In Baku, I basically stayed on the overtake mode for the entire race and therefore I was able to stay with the others,” Perez said.
“But when I overtook them, I was just a passenger because I had no straightline speed. So we have two big issues: load and a lot of drag.
“But we always knew this first year was going to be tricky.”
keyPointsZh: 博塔斯的最快单圈也比佩雷兹慢1.489秒
他因驶入1号弯逃生通道导致能量输出模式混乱，15号弯后刹车失灵撞上护墙
佩雷兹在博塔斯撞车前几乎已经套圈
keyPointsEn: Bottas's fastest single lap was still 1.489s slower than Perez's
His car's deployment pattern got confused after he took the Turn 1 escape road, leaving his rear brakes without effect at Turn 15 where he nosed into the barriers

relatedItems.summaryZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔离开哈斯车队时再度提及“超出自己控制的因素”，暗示这段车手与车队关系的逐渐恶化。哈斯早在夏休期后便通知奥孔大概率不会留队，而法拉利支持的青训车手拉法·卡马拉被认为是接替他的热门人选。
relatedItems.originalTitle: All the reasons the Ocon-Haas relationship fell apart
relatedItems.summaryEn: Esteban Ocon marked his exit from Haas with another reference to elements beyond his control, hinting at a gradual deterioration of the driver-team relationship. Haas decided long ago not to activate its contractual option and informed Ocon shortly after the summer break that he was unlikely to be retained.
keyPointsZh: 哈斯拥有下赛季保留奥孔的合同选择权，但早已决定不激活，并在夏休期后不久通知了他。
法拉利支持的拉法·卡马拉是最热门的接替人选，有人推测是法拉利对其青训车手的支持将奥孔挤出车门。
签约时奥孔是哈斯自2016年车队成立赛季引进罗曼·格罗斯让以来拥有的最成功车手。
keyPointsEn: Haas had a contractual option to retain Ocon for next year, decided long ago not to activate it, and notified him shortly after the summer break.
Ferrari-backed Rafa Camara is the favourite to replace Ocon, leading some to infer Ferrari's support of its junior driver is pushing Ocon out.
When signed, Ocon was the most successful driver Haas had employed since Romain Grosjean, a 10-time podium finisher who joined for the team's inaugural 2016 season.

relatedItems.titleZh: 马来西亚大奖赛回归在即，车手期待雪邦或将上演混乱激战
relatedItems.summaryZh: 阔别近十年后，F1将于2026年重返雪邦，替代被取消的巴林和沙特大奖赛，车手们对这条久未造访的赛道展开了各自的预测。
relatedItems.originalTitle: 'Chaotic racing'? - What F1 drivers expect from Malaysia return
relatedItems.summaryEn: Formula 1 will return to Sepang in 2026 after nearly a decade away, replacing the cancelled Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, and drivers have been sharing their early predictions about the challenge ahead.
keyPointsZh: 大部分车手在阿塞拜疆-马来西亚-新加坡三连赛开始前已在模拟器上为雪邦做了准备
威廉姆斯的模拟数据显示，雪邦在2026年赛道中的能源管理需求约为中等水平，与加拿大和奥地利站相近
世界冠军兰多·诺里斯曾在2017年为迈凯伦车手阿隆索和范多恩担任模拟器支持工作
keyPointsEn: Most drivers had already completed simulator preparations for Sepang before the Azerbaijan-Malaysia-Singapore triple header began
Williams's data places Sepang around average in energy management demands for 2026 circuits, similar to Canada and Austria
World champion Lando Norris provided sim support for McLaren's race drivers Fernando Alonso and Stoffel Vandoorne the last time F1 raced there in 2017
